newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Meyer favours changes for cantonal ban.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Meyer favours changes for cantonal ban.

text.p: Swiss National Bank president Hans Meyer said he favoured changes which would make Switzerland's 24 cantonal banks more competitive, including at least a partial privatisation of such banks.

"Privatisation as a basic principle remains a good idea. Cantons are not ideal owners and a public institution is not the best legal structure for a bank," he said in the text of a welcoming address to the annual meeting of the Swiss Cantonal Bank Association.
The individual banks with their regional business within Switzerland's 26 cantons have a special role as traditional lenders to small and mid-sized firms.
Meyer encouraged them to cooperate, if even only on an organisational level, to allow more diversification and to boost productivity.

Meyer said he mainly shared the views of a Swiss finance ministry expert committee which, in a recent study, said Swiss cantonal governments should be freed from the obligation of backing their respective banks with a full guarantee.
Such changes would be appropriate if the stake held by the respective cantons is reduced in the event of an eventual privatisation.
"We support the goal of giving cantons more flexibility with respect to their relationship to the cantonal banks," Meyer said.
But he opposed lowering the stake held by individual cantons to as low as 10 percent, saying cantons should keep a larger share, perhaps one-third, of the ownership of their respective bank.
Total assets held by the cantonal banks at the end of 1996 totaled 266 billion Swiss francs, according to the Association.
